record.original_question: Are massive-star gamma-ray bursts reliable tracers of the star-formation history of the universe across cosmic time, especially at high redshift?

evidence.quote: Are massive star GRBs good tracers of star formation history of the universe?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Long-duration gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) are believed to originate from the core collapse of certain massive stars. Under the hypothesis that the comoving rate density of such bursts is proportional to the cosmic star-formation rate density (SFRD), one may attempt to use the observed LGRB redshift distribution (corrected for instrumental detection thresholds, beaming, and luminosity function) as a direct tracer of the SFRD ψ(z) of the universe.

Determine whether massive-star (long-duration) gamma-ray bursts are reliable, unbiased tracers of the cosmic star-formation history across all redshifts, and in particular at high redshift (z ≳ 3–4). Specifically: does the comoving LGRB rate density R_GRB(z), inferred from observed samples, satisfy R_GRB(z) ∝ ψ(z) over the full observable redshift range, or is there a systematic, redshift-dependent bias (for example arising from metallicity dependence of the progenitor channel, evolution of the initial mass function, or evolution of LGRB luminosity/beaming properties) that prevents such a proportionality? Quantify any such bias and characterize the redshift regime, if any, in which LGRBs may be used as unbiased tracers of star formation.
artifact.category_tag: Gamma-ray bursts and cosmic star formation
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple studies (2014–2025) have established that long GRBs are biased tracers of star formation, with the bias well explained by a metallicity threshold on progenitors (logOH ≲ 8.55) and possible evolution in LGRB properties (luminosity function, beaming). Under the metallicity-threshold model, LGRBs are expected to become approximately unbiased tracers of the SFRD at z ≳ 3, when most star formation occurs below the metallicity ceiling. However, recent work (2024–2025) indicates additional evolving properties beyond a simple metallicity cut are needed for full reconciliation, so the question is partially resolved rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Long GRBs are Metallicity-biased Tracers of Star Formation
status_evidence.snippet: LGRB host distributions are reconciled with galaxy survey expectations by imposing a metallicity upper limit of logOH ~ 8.55; LGRBs trace SF in an unbiased manner once the bulk of star formation lies below this threshold at z > 3.
status_evidence.claim: LGRBs are metallicity-biased tracers; expected to be unbiased at z>3 under threshold model.

status_evidence.title: Are long gamma-ray bursts biased tracers of star formation? BAT6 sample III
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of host galaxies of complete LGRB sample at z>1 examining stellar masses, SFRs, and metallicities, supporting metallicity-dependent bias.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical evidence for metallicity bias affecting LGRBs as SFR tracers.

status_evidence.title: Probing evolution of Long GRB properties through cosmic formation history
status_evidence.snippet: Beaming angle evolution or simple power-law evolution alone are insufficient; multiple evolving LGRB properties are required to match SFRD.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work shows simple corrections are inadequate; problem is not fully resolved.
